title: Regular base change for closed supported restriction
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, $n\geq1$, $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$, and $h:Y\to X$ a regular morphism of Noetherian schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible. Here regular means flat with geometrically regular fibres (the fibres remain regular after every finite extension of the residue field) [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-regular-scheme, def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Let $a:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], $Z'=Y\times_X Z$, $a':Z'\hookrightarrow Y$, and $h':Z'\to Z$. On small etale bounded-below derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], use exact inverse images [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] and the closed-support right derived functor $a^!$ of $F\mapsto a^{-1}\ker(F\to j_*j^{-1}F)$, with $j$ the open complement [def-pur-etale-supported-kernel]. For every $M\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ the canonical exchange morphism is an isomorphism
$$h'^*a^!M\xrightarrow{\sim}a'^!h^*M.$$
It is natural in $M$ and compatible with shifts, roots-of-unity Tate twists [def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist], open restriction, localization at points, and composition of regular base changes. It is the comparison of the canonical closed-support localization triangles, so it commutes with the closed counits and successive closed supported restrictions. In particular, for $z\in Z$, taking the costalk on $Z$ of $a^!M$ gives the costalk of $M$ at $z$. Here costalk means extraordinary restriction after localization at the point as in [def-per-potential-dualizing-complex]. No constructibility or finite-type assumption on $h$ is imposed.

source.place: Expose XVII, Corollary 4.2.3 and its localization-triangle proof; Lemma 4.3.1.1 (localization and successive supported restrictions).

proof.text: Put $U=X\setminus Z$ and $U'=Y\setminus Z'$ with inclusions $j,j'$, and let $q:U'\to U$ be the projection. Base change preserves the two immersion types. The open complement is indeed $U'$: a point belongs to the inverse image of $U$ precisely when it does not belong to the inverse image of $Z$. The morphism $j$ is quasi-compact, since its inverse image over an affine open of the Noetherian $X$ is an open subscheme of that Noetherian affine and hence quasi-compact. It is quasi-separated: $U\times_XU\cong U$ and its diagonal is the identity, so inverse images of quasi-compact opens under the diagonal are themselves quasi-compact. Thus the direct-image theorem will apply to $j$.

source.place: XVII, proof of Corollary 4.2.3: use the complementary open immersion; qcqs hypotheses of Proposition 4.2.1

proof.text: Write $a^!_0F=a^{-1}\ker(F\to j_*j^*F)$. The support-kernel adjunction identifies $a_*a^!_0F$ with this kernel and gives $a_*\dashv a^!_0$, with $a_*$ exact. Its abelian-sheaf Hom bijection restricts to $\Lambda$-linear maps: for each scalar $t\in\Lambda$, naturality in source and target carries the equation $ft=tf$ to the same equation for the transpose. Kernels and all these maps retain their induced scalar actions, and exact coefficient forgetting detects exactness. Module sheaves have enough injectives. The bounded-below derived-adjunction theorem therefore gives $a_*\dashv a^!=Ra^!_0$ on $D^+$; its counit on an injective representative is the kernel inclusion. The same argument applies to $a'$. This uses the supported functor of the statement, without compactifiability, excellence, or constructibility.

source.place: Tags 09XQ (lemma-sections-with-support-acyclic), support adjunction, and bounded-below derivation

proof.text: Closed pushforward is fully faithful on abelian sheaves, with exact left inverse $a^{-1}$ and counit $a^{-1}a_*\cong1$. The preceding exactness of $a_*$ and exactness of inverse image give the same assertions on $\Lambda$-module sheaves, by forgetting scalars and retaining the scalar action. Localizing this specified exact adjunction termwise gives $a^*\dashv a_*$ on $D^+$ with invertible counit. Its Hom bijection shows that $a_*$ is fully faithful there and reflects isomorphisms. These assertions also hold for $a'_*$. The vanishing $j^*a_*=0$ holds termwise and hence on $D^+$, as does $j'^*a'_*=0$.

source.place: Tag 04CA (proposition-closed-immersion-pushforward), exact adjunction and open-complement vanishing

proof.text: The canonical closed direct-image exchange $c:h^*a_*\to a'_*h'^*$ is invertible. At a geometric point of $Y$ outside $Z'$ both stalks vanish; at a geometric point $z'$ in $Z'$ both stalks identify with the stalk on $Z$ at its image. The inverse-image germ formula and the representative-section description of underived exchange show that the canonical map sends each representative germ to that same germ, so it is the identity under these identifications. Geometric stalk conservativity proves the claim. The identifications are $\Lambda$-linear; applying the exact functors termwise gives $c$ on $D^+$.

source.place: Tags 04CA (proposition-closed-immersion-pushforward) and 03Q1 (lemma-stalk-pullback); canonical map on germs

proof.text:
Choose a bounded-below complex $I$ of injective $\Lambda$-module sheaves representing $M$. For every etale $V\to X$, the restriction-kernel lemma applied to $V\times_XU\hookrightarrow V$ gives surjectivity $I^r(V)\to I^r(V\times_XU)$. Hence $0\to a_*a^!_0I\to I\to j_*j^*I\to0$ is a degreewise short exact sequence. The open immersion $j$ is etale, so $j^*I$ has injective terms. The right-derived injective comparison computes $a^!M$ by $a^!_0I$ and $Rj_*j^*M$ by $j_*j^*I$. The short-exact-complex triangle gives
$$S_M:=a_*a^!M\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_M}M\xrightarrow{\eta_M}Rj_*j^*M\longrightarrow S_M[1].$$
Its arrows are the supported counit and open unit, with the normalization in Step 2. Comparison maps between injective resolutions and naturality of the short-exact-complex triangle make it independent of the resolution and natural in $M$. The identical construction gives the triangle on $Y$.

source.place: Tag 0A45 (lemma-cohomology-with-support-triangle), injective-resolution argument, for bounded-below module complexes

proof.text:
Define $\beta_M:h'^*a^!M\to a'^!h^*M$ to be the transpose under $a'_*\dashv a'^!$ of
$$a'_*h'^*a^!M\xrightarrow{c^{-1}}h^*a_*a^!M\xrightarrow{h^*\varepsilon_M}h^*M.$$
The adjunction bijection gives precisely
$$\varepsilon'_{h^*M}\circ a'_*(\beta_M)\circ c_{a^!M}=h^*\varepsilon_M.$$
Thus this is the prescribed canonical supported exchange, not an arbitrarily chosen isomorphism. The same formula proves naturality in $M$.

source.place: XVII, Corollary 4.2.3: the evident morphism, made explicit by its transpose

proof.text:
Apply regular direct-image base change to $g=j$ and $K=j^*M$. Step 1 checked qcqs of $j$; $h$ is regular between Noetherian schemes and $\ell^n$ is invertible there. It gives an isomorphism
$$E:h^*Rj_*j^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}Rj'_*q^*j^*M\cong Rj'_*j'^*h^*M.$$
The last identification is inverse-image composition for the complementary Cartesian square. No constructibility or finite-type condition on $h$ has been introduced.

source.place: XVII, Proposition 4.2.1 and proof of Corollary 4.2.3, printed p. 281

proof.text:
Apply exact $h^*$ to the triangle of Step 5, obtaining a distinguished triangle $A\to h^*M\to C\to A[1]$, where $A=h^*a_*a^!M$ and $C=h^*Rj_*j^*M$. Compare it with the supported triangle $A'\to h^*M\to C'\to A'[1]$ on $Y$. Step 4 identifies $A$ with $a'_*h'^*a^!M$, so Step 3 gives $j'^*A=0$. The derived adjunction $j'^*\dashv Rj'_*$, obtained by bounded-below derivation of the exact inverse image, gives
$$\operatorname{Hom}(A[k],C')=\operatorname{Hom}(j'^*A[k],j'^*h^*M)=0\quad(k\in\mathbf Z).$$
Here exactness of open inverse image gives its commutation with shifts. The same adjunction applies to module sheaves with transported constant coefficients.

source.place: XVII, localization-triangle proof of Corollary 4.2.3; open adjunction supplies support/open orthogonality

proof.text: Use $\mathrm{id}_{h^*M}$ for the middle comparison, $E$ for the last, and $f=a'_*(\beta_M)c$ for the first. The first square commutes by Step 6. The second square commutes by the definition of derived open exchange as a mate: after transposing under $j'^*\dashv Rj'_*$, the equality $E(h^*\eta_M)=\eta'_{h^*M}$ is the triangle identity $\varepsilon_j\,j^*\eta_j=1$, with inverse-image composition inserted. The coefficient-exchange node specifies that module exchange is formed by these same module adjunctions, so this triangle-identity calculation holds in the module derived category itself. The triangle-extension lemma, applied using $\operatorname{Hom}(A[1],C')=0$ from Step 8, now proves that these specified outer maps form a morphism of distinguished triangles. In particular the connecting square commutes, rather than being inferred from an unspecified cone comparison.

source.place: XVII, proof of Corollary 4.2.3; BBD Proposition 1.1.9 for the normalized comparison of support triangles

proof.text: The middle and last maps of this triangle comparison are isomorphisms (the identity and Step 7). The triangle two-out-of-three lemma makes $f$ an isomorphism. Since $c$ is invertible, $a'_*(\beta_M)$ is invertible. Full faithfulness of $a'_*$ from Step 3 reflects invertibility, proving that $\beta_M$ itself is an isomorphism.

source.place: XVII, proof of Corollary 4.2.3: comparison of the two localization triangles

proof.text: For composition of base changes, the two closed direct-image exchanges send a representative section successively to its restriction twice; this is its restriction along the composite. Thus their composite is the closed exchange of the composite square. Mate pasting along the base-change functors identifies the corresponding composite of $\beta$ with the single composite-square $\beta$. For successive closed immersions $b:W\hookrightarrow Z$ and $a:Z\hookrightarrow X$, direct-image composition identifies $(ab)_*$ with $a_*b_*$, termwise by the fibre-product formula for sections. Right-adjoint composition therefore identifies $(ab)^!$ with $b^!a^!$, with pasted counit. Mate pasting along these adjunctions proves that supported exchange for $ab$ is the successive exchange for $a$ then $b$. The closed counit identity is already Step 6. All these identifications use specified adjunctions, hence their coherence is the pasting identity itself.

source.place: XVII, Corollary 4.2.3 and Lemma 4.3.1.1, canonical comparisons; explicit mate-pasting verification

proof.text: For an etale map $v:V\to X$, inverse image is restriction to objects etale over $V$. Thus $v^*j_*F\cong j_{V,*}v_U^*F$: evaluated on $W\to V$, both are $F(W\times_XU)$. Restricting the supported kernel therefore gives the kernel for the pulled-back closed immersion. Etale restriction preserves injective module sheaves, so the same identity on an injective complex proves etale locality of $a^!$, with its counit normalization. This includes arbitrary open restriction. For localization first work in an affine neighbourhood of the point. The map $\operatorname{Spec}A_{\mathfrak p}\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is affine ind-etale because $A_{\mathfrak p}$ is a filtered colimit of principal localizations; it is Noetherian. Apply ind-etale closed-support base change. Its pullbacks are again affine ind-etale. Together with the open locality just proved, this gives localization for a general ambient $X$. The resulting comparison has the transposed counit of Step 6. Mate pasting in Step 11 proves that these restriction comparisons commute with regular exchange.

source.place: XVII, Lemma 4.3.1.1, localization before the closed-fibre comparison; Tags 03Q9, 09XQ and 0A45 for the ind-etale tool

proof.text: Give exact inverse images and closed pushforwards their termwise shift comparisons. The right-adjoint shift theorem supplies the unique compatible shift comparison for $a^!$ and $a'^!$; on shifted injective complexes it is the usual derived comparison, because the degreewise supported counit is unchanged by shifting. In the transpose formula of Step 6, $c^{-1}$ and $h^*\varepsilon$ commute with these comparisons. Transposing proves $\beta_{M[k]}=\beta_M[k]$ under them, for every integer $k$. This also identifies the shift appearing in the connecting square of Step 9 with the standard cohomological shift.

source.place: XVII, Corollary 4.2.3, derived comparison; shift verification from the adjunction normalization

proof.text: The finite Tate sheaf $L=\Lambda(t)$ is etale locally free of rank one, with dual $L^\vee$ and inverse-image identifications respecting tensor, evaluation and all integer twists. Tensoring with $L$ and $L^\vee$ are inverse exact functors: their evaluation identifications and exactness can be checked on an etale cover where both are the coefficient sheaf. Closed direct image has the sheaf comparison $a_*(N\otimes a^*L)\cong a_*N\otimes L$, which is the identity on such a trivializing cover and whose overlap changes on both sides are multiplication by the same unit. This is an identity of sheaf functors and therefore also of their termwise exact derived functors. Conjugating $a_*\dashv a^!$ by these tensor autoequivalences gives, by right-adjoint uniqueness, $a^!(M\otimes L)\cong a^!M\otimes a^*L$, normalized by its counit. Do the same for the pulled-back closed immersion. In the transpose formula of Step 6 the closed sheaf exchange respects these tensor comparisons, since it restricts representative sections. The two transposes are consequently equal, so the two supported exchanges are equal. This proves twist compatibility globally, including negative twists, with the specified roots-of-unity pullback identifications.

source.place: XVII, Corollary 4.2.3, twist compatibility; Tag 03PK (section-kummer), and conjugation of adjunctions by invertible tensor

proof.text:
Finally take $z\in Z$. On an affine neighbourhood $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ with $Z=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ and prime $\mathfrak p\supset I$, one has
$$Z\times_X\operatorname{Spec}A_{\mathfrak p}=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)_{\mathfrak p/I}=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{Z,z}.$$
Indeed both rings are $A_{\mathfrak p}/IA_{\mathfrak p}$, by the localization tensor formula. Denote this closed map to $X_z=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{X,z}$ by $a_z$ and its closed point inclusion by $b_z$; their composite $a_zb_z$ is the closed point inclusion of $X_z$, with the same residue field. Step 12 gives $(a^!M)|_{Z_z}\cong a_z^!(M|_{X_z})$. Apply $b_z^!$ and then the right-adjoint composition comparison of Step 11:
$$R\Gamma_z^Z(a^!M)=b_z^!((a^!M)|_{Z_z})\cong b_z^!a_z^!(M|_{X_z})\cong(a_zb_z)^!(M|_{X_z})=R\Gamma_z^XM.$$
These are exactly the local-then-supported costalks of the statement. This calculation uses only that costalk recipe, not the excellence or dualizing hypotheses used for the other notions in its definition node. Its normalization is by the successive counits, as required.

source.place: XVII, Lemma 4.3.1.1, successive supported restrictions; costalk definition in Definition 1.1.1

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q47-ed231d1e9 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read ILO XVII 4.2.1 and 4.2.3 (printed p. 281) and Lemma 4.3.1.1. The item statement is unchanged and agrees with Corollary 4.2.3: Z/l^n coefficients, D+, any closed immersion, regular h without finite type or excellence, the canonical mate exchange. The new node lem-per-regular-etale-direct-image-base-change is Proposition 4.2.1 restricted to Noetherian X and Y, with no condition on V and nothing weakened. It is the open-complement input that ILO itself uses, not a clause of the item. A DAG grep found no duplicate: the existing nodes cover only the smooth special case, or 4.2.2 (RHom on excellent schemes, lem-per-potential-regular-base-change). Small cases checked: V empty, g = id, h etale, h a strict localization (not of finite type), Z empty, Z = X, n = 1. All 15 steps check against the statements they cite. Step 5: the module restriction-kernel lemma gives the degreewise short exact supported triangle. Step 9: triangle-extension (2) with Hom(A[1],C') = 0 from Step 8 gives the connecting square. Step 10: two-out-of-three, then a'_* reflects isomorphisms. Step 12: localization goes through an affine open, then ind-etale Spec A_p -> Spec A, so a nonseparated X is handled. Step 15: the costalk matches the R Gamma_x recipe of def-per-potential-dualizing-complex. No SGA citation. Batch-5 flags: lem-trf-bounded-below-derived-adjunction is the generic derivedPlus adjunction; lem-trf-geometric-inverse-image-exact is Stacks 04JC, a topos fact; lem-per-ind-etale-closed-support-base-change reaches sec-trace-formula only through those two and lem-trf-ind-etale-strict-local-invariance (Stacks 05WR, algebra). None is a statement assumed by batch 5 or a step of its proofs, so all three are accepted, consistent with earlier acceptances. The 23 declared tool_uses are generic interfaces and all are accepted.
